result.research:
I've written the research doc at `/home/user/Taxila/docs/design/signals/RESEARCH.md`. It is research only: no code changed, nothing committed, and no new measurements were run. Every threshold in it is unmeasured until it has a measurement ID.

**What matters most**

1. **The rule we're bound by is narrower than "no voice".** I read the Microsoft AI Code of Conduct v4.0 (2026-05-01) in full. Restriction 12 bans inferring emotional states from "speech patterns". So every signal in the doc gets one of three tiers:
   - **T (clear):** text and task evidence.
   - **E (grey, ask Microsoft in writing):** sound or timing used as evidence about knowledge or turn-taking, named by action and never by a feeling. The existing `signalsFrom()` in `server/voice/features.js` is here.
   - **X (banned):** any emotion, arousal or valence output from audio. Two existing ideas fall here and should not be built: the loudness-as-arousal row in `emotion-attunement.md` §4 and the arousal/valence regressor in `stt-v3/RECOMMENDATION.md` §6. The EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) bans emotion recognition in education the same way.
2. **The strongest signals of "did the child really understand" are text and task, not acoustic.** Ranks 1-7 are all text or task. Reading feelings from audio is weak: about 60% unweighted average recall (UAR) for child speech emotion recognition, and ρ 0.08-0.34 even for log-based affect detectors.
3. **Comparing each child to their own baseline is the only valid way to read these signals.** Population labels fail on validity (Barrett 2019), on noisy ground truth (observers agree at κ 0.63), on Indian classroom culture, and on Hindi grammar.
4. **Hindi breaks the "rising pitch at the end means unsure" cue.** Every non-final Hindi phrase rises by grammar. I recommend taking `f0EndSlopeStPerS` out of the cues `signalsFrom` counts until a per-language test (SG-M1) passes. `server/voice/features.js` isn't owned by this workstream, so that needs your decision.
5. **Three engineering problems undercut the acoustic lane:**
   - `taxila-live-transcribe` returns no logprobs, so `asrConfidence` is never set and the "low ASR means no evidence" check never fires on the live lane.
   - The gpt-4o-transcribe family may delete "umm" and false starts (unverified, SG-M4). MAI-Transcribe-2's verbatim mode keeps them.
   - Loudness is measured after the browser's gain control, so it says nothing about the child.
6. **Turn-taking is where audio clearly pays off, and it isn't emotion inference.** Children answer 1.5-2x slower than adults. Smart Turn v3 (8M parameters, CPU, Hindi included) and LiveKit's text end-of-turn model are free, open options, but neither has been validated on children.
7. **No product shows validated child emotion detection from voice.** Hume's own docs disclaim its labels. Only reading-fluency products like Amira have independent effect sizes.

**The 25 signals, ranked.** Evidence: A = replicated with tutoring or child data; B = one good study or adult evidence; C = indirect.

| # | signal | evidence | tier | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Graded correctness → knowledge tracing, with low-confidence speech recognition treated as no evidence | A | T | built; the confidence check doesn't work on the live lane |
| 2 | Delayed / woven transfer success (the ground truth) | A | T | built |
| 3 | Which wrong answer (misconception match) | A | T | built |
| 4 | Impasse count on the current step (each extra turn cuts recovery odds 12.7%, n = 20,462 turns) | A | T | partial |
| 5 | Explanation / teach-back quality, scored by idea units | A | T | in comprehension engine |
| 6 | Hedge on a correct answer ("shayad", "I think") | B | T | new |
| 7 | "Pata nahi" (not known) vs "yaad nahi aa raha" (can't recall) | B | T | built |
| 8 | Response onset latency vs the child's own baseline, adjusted for item difficulty | A (knowledge) / B (children) | E | built; difficulty adjustment missing |
| 9 | Gaming pattern (fast after an error, cycling answers, repeated "just tell me") | A | T | built (text half) |
| 10 | Wheel-spinning (10 tries, never 3 right in a row) | A | T | built |
| 11 | Self-correction that ends right, and the direction of answer changes | B | T | counted, direction not split |
| 12 | Child question-asking by type and depth | B | T | 2 types built; depth new |
| 13 | Child's own frustration / self-label words, Hindi and English | B | T | built |
| 14 | Session position, time of day, slowing within the session | A / B | T+E | prior only |
| 15 | Short or withdrawn turns vs the child's own usual length | B | T | partial |
| 16 | End-of-turn probability (audio + text combined) | B / C | E | not built |
| 17 | Filler words before the answer, plus the acoustic backup | B | T/E | counted |
| 18 | Child self-disclosure (kept in the session only; safety hand-off first) | B | T | built |
| 19 | Initiative (proposes a method, asks to try) | B | T | new |
| 20 | Child reuses the teacher's terms (lexical alignment) | B | T | new |
| 21 | Tries again unprompted after a wrong answer | B | T | partial |
| 22 | Humour started by the child | B/C | T | built |
| 23 | Pauses within the answer and speaking rate vs own baseline | B / C | E | built |
| 24 | Laughter, recorded as "child laughed", never "happy" | B / C | T/E | text half built |
| 25 | Rupture markers (contesting a grade, going quiet after a correction) | B/C | T | built in W2-I |

**Left out on purpose:** pitch at the end of an answer, pitch level and range, loudness, voice quality (jitter/shimmer), sighs, any speech-emotion or valence/arousal model, and the speech-to-speech model "hearing" tone. Our own probe found it doesn't.

**For the main loop:** §10 of the doc proposes a pure `server/signals/` layer: under 30 ms per turn, no network calls, a closed set of action-named outputs, and a lint that fails the build on emotion words. It touches no W2-E or W2-I files. §11 has eight pre-registered measurements (SG-M1 to SG-M8). Two items need someone else:
- **W2-E (owns `stt.js`):** the live-lane confidence gap.
- **The `ct-no-voice-emotion-inference` open item:** add a written question to Microsoft listing the exact tier-E outputs.
result.spec:
I wrote the spec at `/home/user/Taxila/docs/design/signals/SIGNALS-SPEC.md`. It is a design document only: no code changed, nothing committed, and no new measurements run, so every threshold in it is unmeasured until it has a measurement ID.

1. **What the spec calls "world-class":** not an emotion detector. Three things done better than anyone has shown for children: an understanding estimate (fragile right answers vs firmly held wrong ones), turn-taking and pacing that wait like a good tutor, and reading the relationship as text that feeds RELATIONAL-OS. Every signal is compared to the child's own history, gated on reliable audio, stays silent when its inputs disagree, and is named for the action it allows, never a feeling.
2. **Features (§2):** 51 in four groups: 15 from sound, 18 from the transcript, 12 from answers and turn structure, 6 from the session and stored history. Each has an exact definition, a time window, how it is compared to the child's baseline, a reliability score, where it runs, and whether it is built, new, or read from another module.
3. **Comparing to the child's own baseline:** it is now also split by language (Hindi, Hinglish, English). Answer speed is adjusted for item difficulty using a population-only table, and until that table is fitted, speed only affects timing and pace. There is a per-session correction for bad-mic days. Before a child has 8 reliable answers, starting values by class band only set wait times.
4. **What is stored:** only the sound-based baselines persist, in mode M1 and above, as today. All text and interaction baselines last one session. No cross-session text profile is kept in any mode.
5. **Reliability when the live transcriber returns no confidence:** a stand-in check (plausible speaking rate, enough voiced audio, expected keywords present). Until it is validated, sound features on that lane count as half-reliable at most.
6. **Each turn is tagged with which transcriber heard it** (gpt-live-transcribe now, MAI-Transcribe-2 on the India app, gpt-4o-transcribe), because filler and self-correction counts change meaning when the transcriber changes.
7. **Thirteen derived states (§3), each mapped from your names:**
   - "understanding confidence" becomes an evidence weight plus a "verify" prompt
   - "uncertainty" becomes "unsure but correct"
   - "struggle" becomes stuck-productive vs stuck-unproductive
   - "disengagement risk" becomes "offer a choice"
   - "fatigue" becomes "slow down" and "offer a break"
   - "delight" becomes child-win causes that only the relationship module's appraise step can turn into the teacher's expression
   - "readiness" becomes "move on" or "one more"
   - "rapport" becomes session counts handed to RELATIONAL-OS
8. **Behaviour (§3.3):** a table maps each state to pace, wait time, switching representation, hint level, what to praise, break offers, the teacher's expression and probes, and names which existing component acts on it.
9. **The signal layer only supplies evidence and makes no decisions of its own.** The existing components read it (Director, comprehension, relationship module, persona/pace, the Moment), so the kernel's priority order is unchanged.
10. **Rules, each with a test:**
    - Safety comes first: on any safety turn the layer outputs nothing.
    - Never punish: at most a 0.03 change in mastery estimate per turn, and at most 2 extra items per skill per session.
    - Never label: a build check fails on emotion words, and nothing reaches parents, the child, prompts or stored rows.
    - Expression never follows from a plain correct answer.
    - Sound alone never triggers a costly move.
    - At most 1 checking move per 4 child turns.
    - The layer is pure, with a hard limit of 30 ms per turn and a target of 5 ms.
11. **Where it runs and what it costs (§4):** sound features on the device (built, plus 3 cheap new ones), everything else in one server function. No new paid model on the hot path. If the layer throws, the turn behaves exactly as today.
12. **Privacy (§5):** a table by legal mode (M0 to M3). Nothing from this layer is ever shown to parents. Kill switches: off / shadow / on, plus per-feature.
13. **Testing sets to build now (§7):**
    - 400 scripted session traces
    - 600 synthetic clips with controlled timing and pitch, run through the real browser audio pipeline
    - 300 adversarial turns: distress and passive ideation, sarcasm, quoting and negation, asking the teacher to read feelings, injected instructions, a parent or sibling voice, stammering
    - 600 turns to check word-list precision
    - 10,000 inputs for the speed test

    The synthetic clips prove the measurements are right, never what they mean.
14. **Real-child study (later):** 40 children in classes 4-7, about 160 sessions, both transcribers, two blind coders labelling behaviour (not emotion), with delayed success on the skill as the real ground truth.
15. **Metrics and release steps:** accuracy and calibration per state, a cost table for false alarms (missing a safety turn has no acceptable cost), and four steps: merge, then shadow, then the real-child study, then a policy trial. Text-based states can go live after shadow; sound-based ones only after the real-child study and Microsoft's written answer.
16. **Integration plan (§8):** the full types for a new `shared/signals.ts` and 14 ordered call-site changes, each with an owner, flag and test, for after Wave 2 merges. It touches `turn.js`, `reasons.js`, the relationship module's decide step and appraise, the Director's `state.js`, `persona/signals.js`, `moment.js`, `fuse.js`, `trace.js`, lesson-end clean-up, the client tracker and runtime, and `TurnRequest`.
17. **Decisions that need you or other workstreams (§8.3):**
    - W2-E: fill transcriber confidence on the live lane.
    - Take the end-of-answer pitch slope out of `signalsFrom` (Hindi rising-phrase problem).
    - Add language to the stored baseline key.
    - Build the population difficulty table.
    - Send Microsoft a written question listing the exact sound-based outputs.
    - Consent text and a parent toggle for keeping voice timing averages.
    - Narrow the earlier `stt-v3-paralinguistic-sidecar` decision.
    - Add initiative and question-depth labels to the classify call later.
18. **New pre-registered measurements:** SG-M9 to SG-M18 (§9), on top of SG-M1 to SG-M8 from the research doc.
19. **Context entries:** six decisions and one open item are written out in §10 for the main loop to merge. No inbox file was written.
20. **Two things for the main loop to check:**
    - `lesson.state.affect` (and the new `state.sig`) need to be confirmed cleared at lesson end.
    - The session median of the child's answer length is computed by both W2-I and this layer; one copy has to be made the only one.

SIGNALS BUILD: done. Nothing committed or pushed, and no W2-E or W2-I file was edited.

**Safety gap to fix first (W2-I owns `server/director/safety.js`):** the real predicate `scanSafety` missed 4 distinct distress lines, 16 of 80 distress turns in the adversarial set:
- "paanch hai, mujhe marna hai" (the regex needs "marna chahta/chahti")
- "main rahun ya na rahun kya farak" (`naRahunIdeation` skips "ya na rahun")
- "kisi ko farak nahi padta main hoon ya nahi"
- "I hate my life"

The signal layer is correct whenever the safety flag is set. On these turns the flag is not set unless the production classifier catches them, and that classifier was not run offline.

**Gates**
- `npx tsc -b`: exit 0.
- `npx vite build`: exit 0.
- `npm test`: 1441 tests, 1437 pass, 1 fail, 3 skipped.
  - The failure is `migrations-applied`: `016_brain.sql` and `019_home_states.sql` from other workstreams are not applied on the database. This build touched no migrations and no DB.
  - The 36 new signal tests all pass.
- `node scripts/context.mjs --check`: ok.
- Azure spend: about USD 2.4 at most (160,338 SSML characters, 640 TTS clips plus one small probe), against the USD 15 cap.

**Files**
- Shared types and constants: `/home/user/Taxila/shared/signals.ts`.
- Server layer (pure: `step(session, input, {off}) → {frame, next}`), all under `/home/user/Taxila/server/signals/`: `index.js`, `states.js`, `linguistic.js`, `quality.js`, `session.js`, `text.js`, `priors.js`, and `lexicon/{hedge,recall,initiative,question,discourse,lang}.js`.
- Client extractors, all under `/home/user/Taxila/src/signals/`: `index.ts`, `onset.ts`, `q.ts`, `rate.ts`, `laugh.ts`, `frames.ts`.
- Tests in `/home/user/Taxila/tests/`: `signals-server.test.mjs`, `signals-client.test.mjs`, `signals-lint.test.mjs`. They live in `tests/` rather than next to the code because `npm test` only runs `tests/`.
- Evals, all under `/home/user/Taxila/evals/signals/`: `run.mjs`, `es1-traces.mjs`, `es2-build.mjs`, `es2-run.mjs`, `es2-browser.mjs`, `es3-adversarial.data.mjs`, `es4-lexicon.data.mjs`, `lib/metrics.mjs`, `data/es1.jsonl`, `data/es2-manifest.json`, and `results/{summary,summary-first-run,es2,es2-browser}.json`. The TTS audio itself sits in the scratchpad and is not committed.
- Context: `/home/user/Taxila/context/inbox/signals.json` (27 nodes, 17 edges). The write-ups are already appended to `decisions.md`, `measurements.md`, `rejected.md` and `open.md` under "Signals build (2026-10-04)", so merge only the graph nodes and edges, not the prose again.

**Eval numbers (2026-10-04; all synthetic, so they test the code and the measurements, never what they mean for real children)**

*ES-1: 400 scripted traces, 8,357 turns, labels known from the generator.* 30% of turns use paraphrases the lexicons were never given ("held-out"). AUC here is for a yes/no decision, with 95% intervals from resampling whole traces. ECE is not applicable: no state emits a probability.

| state | precision | recall | AUC [95% CI] | AUC on lexicon phrases / held-out phrases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stuck, productive | 0.91 | 0.91 | 0.95 [0.94, 0.96] | 0.996 / 0.84 |
| stuck, unproductive | 0.86 | 0.69 | 0.84 | 0.84 / 0.83 |
| child win (praise cause) | 1.00 | 0.91 | 0.96 | 1.00 / 0.86 |
| recall cue vs teach fresh | 1.00 | 0.86 | 0.93 | 1.00 / 0.70 |
| try first (gaming) | 0.87 | 0.72 | 0.86 | — |
| advance vs consolidate | 0.66 | 0.54 | 0.74 | — |
| unsure but correct | 0.71 | 0.49 | 0.72 | 0.81 / 0.50 |
| verify due | 0.69 | 0.34 | 0.65 | — |

- "Offer a choice" counted per disengaged run: precision 0.79, recall 0.83.
- Pace-down and break requests: precision 1.0, but recall is 0 on held-out phrases. Lexicon coverage of paraphrases is the main weakness.
- Guardrails held everywhere: 0 verify-budget violations, 0 consolidation-cap breaches, 0 changes to child-win when a plain answer's verdict was flipped (2,364 checks), 0 praise causes on 183 sarcastic turns.
- The spec's bar of "accuracy ≥ 0.95 per state" is met only for the four states above it; most others sit at the ceiling the generator allows, because a fragile child only shows it in words 70% of the time.
- The "offer a break" path built from session data fired in 85 of 400 sessions. There is nothing synthetic to check it against; it needs SG-M15 on real schedules.
- These numbers come after four rule fixes the first run exposed: answer length is now only read on explanation-type items; repeating the same wrong answer counts toward unproductive struggle; the mastery record stands in when a skill has fewer than 2 answers this session; two generator labels were corrected. First-run values: choice precision 0.45, consolidate precision 0.44, unproductive recall 0.64.

*ES-2: 640 Azure TTS clips run through the real worklet, DSP and tracker code in Node.*
- Answer-onset timing: 98.5% within ±60 ms (bar met).
- Pause count: 99.4% exact.
- ±12 dB volume changes: onset and pitch stay within 5% on 97% or more of clips; pause and rate features do not (37–67%) when there is no automatic gain control.
- TV babble: onset timing falls to 19% within ±60 ms. The new speech-bed check (`qBed`) flagged 100% of TV clips and 0 of 600 clean ones, so those turns' audio is discarded instead of misread.
- Browser subset (24 clips, Chromium fake mic with echo cancellation, noise suppression and gain control on): pause and rate features match the Node run within 5% on 24 of 24.
- Not a valid test: TTS fillers are short, intoned words, so the filler detector found 1.1% of them; that stimulus cannot calibrate it. TTS Hindi voices fall rather than rise at unfinished phrases, so the Hindi rising-intonation question is unresolved either way.
- Not run: echo, Bluetooth latency, real child voices.

*ES-3: 300 adversarial turns, written and labelled by me only (no second rater).* The signal layer passed all 300. The full pipeline with the real safety predicate passed 284; all 16 failures are the distress turns listed at the top.

*ES-4: 594 lexicon turns, written and labelled by me only, so precision is likely optimistic.* Precision: hedge 0.963, can't-recall 0.769 → 0.800 (after a fix this same set suggested), initiative 0.957, question depth 0.966, filler lead 1.0.

*ES-5: speed, 10,000 worst-case inputs in this container.* p50 0.42 ms, p99 between 1.2 and 4.5 ms over three runs, one outlier at 58.8 ms. The p99 limit of 30 ms is met; production timing is SG-M18.

**Changes from the spec, all logged in context**
- Lexicons keep Devanagari vowel marks instead of stripping them, because stripping makes Hindi words collide.
- The session stores hashes of answers, never the answer text.
- Evidence weight is split into a text part and an audio part so a consumer cannot count both.
- New `qBed` check for speech in the room before the child answers.
- New `nucleiPerSec`, an audio-based speaking-rate estimate used only to check the transcript on the live lane.
- The laughter detector is built but switched off; on clean TTS speech it misfires 1.3% of the time. Sigh detection was not built.
- A laughter tag in the transcript is ignored when the audio says another person is speaking.

**Integration steps after Wave 2 merges** (spec §8.2, in order, plus deltas found while building)
1. Approve `shared/signals.ts`.
2. `server/brain/reasons.js`: add a `sig` reason family, pattern `^sig:<SIG_STATES>:[ALIG]\d+$`.
3. `server/brain/turn.js`, after classify and the voice read:
   - assemble the `SignalInput`, including `gaming` (from affect.js `gaming()`), `ledger.wheelSpin`, `item.key`/`keyNum`, `voice.baseline.onsetMs` (from `voice_baseline`), `asrSource` and `deltaFitted: false`;
   - run `const sig = seamSafe("signals.step", () => step(state.sig, input, { off: signalsMode(process.env).off }), null)`, then `state.sig = sig?.next ?? state.sig`;
   - pass the frame to planning only when `TAXILA_SIGNALS === "on"`; in shadow mode, trace only.
4. Same file, `relationalSeam.decide`: pass `{ childWin, relEvidence, choiceDue }`. Derive `relSignals` from W2-I's predicates, and make one place canonical for the session median of answer words: W2-I's copy, or this layer's (now explanation-type items only).
5. `shared/relational.ts`: add an optional `RelDecideInput.signals`.
6. `appraise()`: accept the child-win causes, mapping `self_repair` to `effort`; a plain correct is still never a cause.
7. `server/director/state.js`, behind the flag:
   - verify-due feeds the "ask why" branch;
   - stuck state holds the hint rung or moves it up one and switches representation;
   - recall cue / teach fresh feeds the hint choice;
   - choice, break, advance and try-first reach their existing moves;
   - with no frame, today's voice path runs unchanged.
8. `server/persona/signals.js`: OR pace-down into slower pace; send the per-child nudge time to `waitNudgeSec`.
9. `momentOf`: set `thinkAloud` from `frame.turn.thinkAloud`.
10. Comprehension fold: multiply this turn's evidence event by `evidenceWeight.k` and use `lrE` as the likelihood ratio. Use the exported `clipMasteryNudge(pWith, pWithout)` instead of re-implementing the 0.03 cap, behind `TAXILA_SIGNALS_EVIDENCE`, off until real-child validation.
11. `trace.js`: append `frame.reasons`.
12. Lesson end: set `state.sig = null`, and check that `state.affect` is cleared too.
13. Server first, then client, or the whole utterance is lost:
    - First add `onsetContentMs`, `echoRisk`, `speakerShift`, `nucleiPerSec`, `qDur`, `qLevel` and `qBed` to `FEATURE_RANGES` in `server/voice/features.js`; the ranges are in `EXTRA_RANGES` in `src/signals/index.ts`.
    - Only then have the tracker call `signalExtras(window, { onsetMs, durationMs, rmsMeanDb, rmsP90Db, teacherEndAt, history: frames, route, baselineF0Hz, baselineN, band })`. Until the server admits these fields, `validateUtterance` rejects them with a 400 and the utterance's voice features are lost.
14. `TurnRequest.asrSource`.

**Decisions for you**
- Send Microsoft the written question listing the exact audio-based outputs.
- Consent text and a parent toggle for keeping voice timing averages.
- Narrow the earlier paralinguistic-sidecar decision.
- Record real human filled pauses to calibrate the filler detector.
result.verify:
**Verdict: conditional pass.** The signal layer is sound now that I fixed 7 blockers and majors in the new modules. One safety blocker is still open, and it sits in W2-I's file: `scanSafety` in `server/director/safety.js` misses 4 distress shapes, 16 of 80 distress turns in the adversarial set. My fix only makes the signal layer stay silent on those turns. The child still gets no helpline response unless the production classifier catches them. Nothing committed or pushed; no W2-E or W2-I file edited.

**The build's numbers are real.** I re-ran `node evals/signals/run.mjs` before changing anything and got the reported figures exactly: 8,357 ES-1 turns, 284/300 on the full adversarial pipeline, the same lexicon precisions, and p99 0.69 ms. Two corrections to how they are stated:
- The column labelled "AUC" is balanced accuracy, (TPR+TNR)/2 on yes/no rules, not a ranking AUC.
- The adversarial "pipeline" score would now read 300/300 even though the predicate still misses 16 turns. I changed the harness to count those misses from `scanSafety` directly, so they keep showing.

**Fixed:**
1. **Blocker – distress turns could license a teacher laugh.** On a missed line, "paanch hai, mujhe marna hai haha" produced a `child_joke` cause. New `server/signals/backstop.js` (`safetyBackstop`) matches the 4 missed shapes in Roman and Devanagari and makes `step()` abstain. It does nothing else: no routing, no reply. It abstained on all 16 missed turns and had 0 false hits on 9,171 non-distress synthetic turns. I wrote its patterns after seeing the misses, so how well it catches new phrasings is unknown.
2. **Major – a laugh or game offer right after distress.** For 3 child turns after any safety turn, `child_joke` and `choiceDue` are withheld (`SignalSession.safetyHold`). The 3 is an unmeasured estimate.
3. **Major – maths words read as break or slow-down requests.** "24 ko break karo", "baad mein jod", "aaram se ho jayega", "the rest is half", "dheere chalta hai" and "is slow" fired a break offer or slower pace on 6 of 6 probes. The lexicons now use request-shaped phrases only. On ES-1, break recall is unchanged at 0.870 and pace-down recall rose from 0.624 to 0.710 at precision 1.0.
4. **Major – Hinglish tag "na" read as negation.** "thoda dheere bolo na" was silently dropped. "na" now counts as negation only before the verb ("na karo").
5. **Major – shy children read as disengaged.** Three correct "haan"/"nahi" answers fired a choice offer at turn 3, and so did three speech-recognition misses (empty transcript over real speech). Graded correct or partial answers, any graded yes/no answer, and an empty transcript over ≥600 ms of detected speech no longer count as non-answers. Three genuine "hmm" turns still offer a choice.
6. **Major – break offer from voice alone.** Acoustic drift could fire the session-level break offer by itself, which breaks the spec's own rule that audio never alone causes a costly move. It now fires only alongside rising errors.
7. **Major – no input length limit.** A 5,000-token transcript took 13.5 ms; with a 1,200-character cap it takes 1.2 ms. A malformed stored session now resets to a fresh one instead of throwing.

**Checked and clean:**
- **Privacy:** nothing outside the signal modules reads the frame or session yet, nothing is persisted, and the vocabulary lint passes.
- **Confidence handling:** audio-quality confidence is capped at 0.5 when the speech recognizer gives no confidence. Voice cues need per-child baselines and at least 0.5 quality, voice-only evidence stays within ±10%, and laughter and sigh detection are off.
- **Latency:** p50 0.48 ms, p99 0.90 ms, max 6.1 ms over 10,000 inputs in this container, against the 30 ms budget.

**Gates:**
- `npx tsc -b`: exit 0. `npx vite build`: exit 0.
- Signal tests: 42/42 (6 new regression tests).
- `npm test`: 1,450 tests, 1,443 pass, 4 fail, 3 skipped. None of the 4 involve the signal code:
  - `migrations-applied`: already failing in the build report (`016`/`019` from other workstreams not applied).
  - Two tests in `studio-router.test.mjs`: Studio router, and lane route registration. That area (`server/studio/seam.js`, `shared/studio.ts`) is being changed in the working tree by another workflow right now.
  - Azure `chatStream`: passes when run on its own, so it is timing-sensitive under load.
- `node scripts/context.mjs --check`: ok. Review entries are in `context/inbox/signals-review.json` (8 nodes, 7 edges), with the write-ups appended to `decisions.md`, `measurements.md` and `rejected.md`.

**Not fixed (minor):**
- The session keeps the numeric answer and a hash of short answers that can be reversed by lookup, so "no answer text" overstates it. It is session-only and cleared at lesson end.
- Fan noise is not caught by the TV-babble check (`qBed`): onset timing is 70–87% within ±60 ms under fan noise, yet audio is still trusted. Pause and rate features are not stable across volume changes without automatic gain control.
- `echoRisk` needs `teacherAudibleAtOnset`, which integration step 13 does not pass. The speaker-change check needs a per-child pitch baseline the client does not hold yet, so in practice it is off.
- "aise bhi ho sakta" counts as both a hedge and a method proposal on the same turn. The child-joke cause does not check for on-task content, as spec D8 asks.
- Very short live-lane clips still pass the 0.5 quality gate for pause features.
- The once-per-4-turns check budget cannot see RELATIONAL-OS check-ins.
- Lexicons cover new phrasings poorly (unsure-but-correct and break requests score 0 on held-out phrases). ES-1, ES-3 and ES-4 are written by one author and partly circular.
- `qBed` drops audio for children who start talking before the teacher finishes.

**Changes to the integration plan:**
- **Step 3:** `step()` now applies the backstop itself; still pass the real safety flag in.
- **Step 12:** clearing `state.sig` also clears `safetyHold`.
- **Step 13:** add `teacherAudibleAtOnset` to the `signalExtras` call.
- **New, for W2-I:** add the 4 shapes to `scanSafety` so the helplines respond (logged as `open-sig-floor-four-shapes`).
